name: callrail
description: Work with CallRail calls, text messages, and form submissions through its REST API.
---

# CallRail

CallRail access is provided through `CALLRAIL_API_KEY`; `CALLRAIL_API_BASE_URL`
defaults to `https://api.callrail.com/v3`. Do not print, log, or write the key.

Send `Authorization: Token token="$CALLRAIL_API_KEY"` on each request. Validate
access safely by listing accounts before reading an account's data:

```bash
printf 'header = "Authorization: Token token=\"%s\""\n' "$CALLRAIL_API_KEY" | \
  curl -sS --fail-with-body "${CALLRAIL_API_BASE_URL:-https://api.callrail.com/v3}/a.json" -K -
```

The v3 API reads calls, text messages, and form submissions beneath an account:
`/a/{account_id}/calls.json`, `/a/{account_id}/text-messages.json`, and
`/a/{account_id}/form_submissions.json`.

1. Start read-only and state the account you will inspect.
2. Never expose API keys or caller-sensitive data unnecessarily.
3. On 401 or 403, ask the user to reconnect with a valid CallRail API key.

Import flow: **File → Map columns → Review → Import**. Mapping auto-suggests fields by header label/key, blocks duplicate column assignments, warns on unmapped required fields that still need a spreadsheet value, and cycles sample values across the first five parsed rows. Fields marked `generated` or with a `defaultValue` do not block mapping — create/import fills them when omitted. Duplicate handling: **create**, **skip**, or **update** with a match field (for example email). When skip or update is selected, the dialog fetches existing records on demand (`fetchAllCollectionRecordsForImport`) before preview counts — create mode does not need that fetch. Before writing rows, Import repairs invalid physical `field.column` values (for example spreadsheet labels with spaces) into snake_case identifiers so storage create does not fail with a raw identifier error.

CSV parsing uses **PapaParse** (RFC 4180 quoted fields and embedded newlines). Export and re-import round-trip is the primary manual regression for multiline cell values.

Progress toasts cover long import/export jobs (`CollectionImportToast`, `CollectionExportDownloadToast`).

## Synced collections

Integration sync (Phase 6) mirrors provider objects into org-scoped **Synced collections** (`kind: virtual`). Registered sync modules: **Apollo**, **Attio**, **Cal.com**, **GitHub**, **Housecall Pro**, **HubSpot**, **Jobber**, **Linear**, **Mercury**, **Notion**, **Printavo**, **QuickBooks**, **Salesforce**, **Shopmonkey**, **Slack**, **Todoist**, and **Wave** (`module-manifest.ts`).

| Surface | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Settings → Integrations → **Settings** | Enable/disable sync per object; stop with keep or delete data; OAuth upgrade when sync scopes are missing. Restricted objects show an exception-only hint (no Add and/or no Delete) — full CRUD objects stay quiet. |
| GitHub sync settings | **Repository access** — all repositories or a selected list; scopes inbound sync and webhooks. An empty selected list is valid and syncs zero rows. In **all repositories** mode, a periodic ETag probe registers webhooks on newly accessible repos (~30 minutes). Repositories are update-only in Genesis (no Add/Delete); Name/URL/identity fields are read-only — only description and private push outbound. Issues and pull requests support create/update; Delete closes them (GitHub REST has no hard delete). |
| Jobber sync | Updates arrive on a periodic schedule (Jobber has no per-account webhooks). **Clients** mirror primary email/phone plus full email/phone JSON from Jobber; **Jobs** mirror `billing_frequency` for recurring cadence. Properties, quotes, jobs, and invoices cannot be deleted (no GraphQL delete/archive). Clients and requests archive on Delete; visits hard-delete. |
| Housecall Pro sync | Customers, employees, leads, jobs, estimates, and invoices. Webhooks cover customers/leads/jobs/estimates/invoices; employees poll. Outbound: customers and jobs full CRUD; leads/estimates/invoices create-only; employees read-only. Partner OAuth required (`handler_kind: housecallpro`). |
| Linear sync | Labels, projects, cycles, and issues support full create/update/delete. Delete archives projects/cycles/issues and hard-deletes labels. |
| Attio sync | Every workspace object from Attio’s catalog supports create/update/delete via the records API. |
| Apollo sync | Lists, accounts, contacts, opportunities, sequences, and tasks. Inbound is poll-only (no CRM webhooks). Most objects are create/update without hard delete; sequences archive on Delete. |
| Cal.com sync | Schedules, event types, and bookings with webhooks when Platform OAuth includes webhook scopes. Booking delete cancels via the provider API. |
| HubSpot sync | Contacts, companies, deals, tickets, products, and line items with app-level webhooks. Full create/update/delete (delete archives). |
| Mercury sync | Accounts (read-only), transactions (update-only), recipients, and cards. Webhooks cover transactions and account balance; recipients/cards poll. |
| Notion sync | Each shared database (data source) becomes a syncable object. Inbound is poll-only; full CRUD on pages/rows when the provider allows. |
| Salesforce sync | Accounts, contacts, leads, and opportunities. Inbound uses the Salesforce Pub/Sub CDC bridge when enabled (#699 / TAC-611), with outbound event webhooks as a fallback path. Full create/update/delete (delete archives). |
| Slack sync | Users (read-only), channels, and messages. Inbound is poll-only (workspace user tokens cannot install Events API hooks). |
| Todoist sync | Projects, labels, sections, tasks, and comments. Inbound is poll-only; full CRUD on supported objects. |
| Wave sync | Invoices only. Inbound is poll-only; outbound create/update/delete via GraphQL mutations (`invoice:write` scope). Create requires a Wave `customerId` and line item `productId`; write status is `DRAFT` or `SAVED` only — marking paid uses payment APIs, not `invoicePatch`. `invoice:send` remains out of scope. Business id resolves from sync metadata or the first accessible Wave business. |
| Shopmonkey sync | Customers, vehicles, orders, users, appointments, vendors, purchase orders, inspections, inventory (parts/tires/labor/fees), and payments. Inbound prefers Shopmonkey webhooks (HMAC-signed) with poll fallback. Connect uses a Shopmonkey API key (Bearer), not OAuth. Users cannot be deleted; payments are read-only. |
| CallRail sync | Calls, text messages, and form submissions. Inbound polls the CallRail v3 API. Connect uses a CallRail API key (`Authorization: Token token="API_KEY"`), not OAuth. The synced collections are read-only. |
| QuickBooks sync | Customers, invoices, and payments (v1 AR surface). Inbound is poll + app-level Intuit webhooks (`poll_and_webhook`): paste the Catalyst URL into Developer Portal → Webhooks and set `GENESIS_QUICKBOOKS_WEBHOOK_VERIFIER_TOKEN`. Outbound create/update/delete via the Accounting REST API; invoice create needs `customer` + `item_id` + `amount`. Company realm resolves from Ion OAuth `realmId` / sync metadata; non-production broker rows use the sandbox API host. |
| Printavo sync | First-party **API-key** connect (not broker OAuth). Customers, contacts, inquiries, statuses, quotes, invoices, tasks, products, transactions, and users. Inbound is poll-only (Printavo has no HTTPS webhooks). Outbound CRUD follows declared `operations` per entity — contacts/quotes/invoices have create limits where Printavo requires parent references Genesis cannot write yet. Catalog: `tools/genesis/api-key-providers/printavo.json`; adapter: `integrations/sync/printavo/` (#824 / TAC-807). |
| Collection records table | Sync attribution banner; lock icons on read-only mirrored columns; Add/Delete/import create respect per-object outbound operations |
| Collection settings | Synced fields (schema-managed) vs your local extension fields; links back to integration sync settings |
| Record edit sheet | Read-only mirrored columns are disabled; writable mirror fields still push outbound via CDC |

Bidirectional sync is always on when an object is enabled — there is no separate outbound toggle. Failed outbound pushes requeue automatically (debounced in-process retry + periodic sweeper). User-facing copy uses **Synced collection**, never “virtual” or “mirror.”

**Inbound run recovery (#917):** manual sync runs that lose their worker (for example
when the HTTP request's app process stops mid-pull) are marked `failed` with
`execution_abandoned` after a short stale window (default five minutes,
`GENESIS_INTEGRATION_SYNC_STALE_RUN_MS`) instead of staying in **Syncing**
indefinitely. The durable poller retries automatically. Provider pull failures
and abandoned runs surface entity `error` status; user pause still maps to
`paused`. Integration disconnect clears sync state without wedging when optional
provider teardown (for example Jobber app disconnect) cannot refresh a broken token.

**New integration adapters** must ship in a single end-to-end PR: all sync-eligible objects, declared outbound create/update/delete per object (full CRUD by default; provider limits declared on the entity), and webhooks when the provider supports them. See **`.agents/skills/genesis-integration-sync/references/shipping-standard.md`**.

Adapter work uses skill **`genesis-integration-sync`** (`.agents/skills/genesis-integration-sync/`) and local rules in `apps/web/src/integrations/sync/AGENTS.md`. Generic API routes live under `/api/integration-sync/*` (`integration-sync.ts`).

### Outbound record operations

Adapters declare per-object outbound create/update/delete on `RemoteEntityDescriptor.operations` (omitted fields default to allowed). Genesis exposes the normalized flags on `CollectionSyncSource.operations` and enforces them in four layers:

| Layer | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Records UI | Hide Add / Delete / import-create when the operation is not allowed; attribution banner may note the limit |
| API + Hub tools | Reject create/delete (and remote-field updates when update is disallowed) with a clear validation error |
| Outbound CDC | Do not call `pushRecordChange` for a disallowed operation; mark the entity/row failed with the same message |
| Adapter client | Keep `not_supported` throws as defense in depth |

Declared limits (everything else defaults to full CRUD):

| Integration | Object | Create | Update | Delete |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GitHub | Repositories | no | yes | no |
| GitHub | Issues, pull requests | yes | yes | yes (closes) |
| Jobber | Properties, quotes, jobs, invoices | yes | yes | no |
| Jobber | Clients, requests, visits | yes | yes | yes (archive / visitDelete) |
